findings.problem: For money owed, Germans almost always say the plural die Schulden, so a learner who knows German well would likely answer that, and the hint doesn't tell them to give the singular dictionary form.
findings.fix: hint: money you owe; give the singular, though it's mostly used in the plural (Schulden)

back.target: debt (also guilt, fault); for money owed it's nearly always the plural, Schulden
back.example: He owes the bank a lot of money (literally: he has many debts with the bank).

note: The English line of the example could sound more natural, for example "He owes the bank a lot of money" or "He's deep in debt to the bank".
